$comment: The authored part of grimoire v11. Everything else is generated by build_v11.py from its sources. DRAFT: the First Person edits this file; build_v11.py is re-run after every edit. Every errata quote is checked verbatim against its source at build time.
subtitle: From spellbook to evidence
tagline: Privacy is value. Take back the 7th capital.
author: privacymage
license: Open for sovereignty, closed to surveillance
description: Grimoire v11 is the first grimoire of the whole agentprivacy universe. It joins the two lines that came before it: the Privacymage Grimoire (last pinned at v10.4.0, 9 June 2026) and the City of Mages Grimoire (last pinned at v1.9.3, 13 July 2026). It does not copy their tales. They are immutable on IPFS and are named here by CID, so the lore stands exactly as it was published. Instead v11 records what the four months since then made: the tomes that went on being written, the master chronicles, the mages whose work is sealed as κ evidence, the scrolls and quests that carry those seals, the proverbs, and the corrections the conjecture register has made to things the earlier grimoires said. Every entry names its source file and that file's sha256 at build time, so the grimoire can be checked against the record it summarises.
how_to_read: Lore before July 2026 is held by reference. Read it in the pinned predecessors; this grimoire gives the CID and the JSON path.
Every generated entry carries source (a path relative to the keeper's home) and source_sha256. A reader with the repositories can re-derive it.
Status words are literal. Bound, draft, proposed: the tome's own record. Signed, unsigned: whether the First Person has read and signed the master chronicle.
An unsigned chronicle appears by date and title only. Its inversion enters the grimoire when it is signed.
A seal is a hash. Scrolls and quests show roots, never results; the veil holds here as it holds on mages.city.

Where the register has corrected an earlier grimoire, the correction is in errata with both quotes, checked word for word at build time. The earlier text is not edited, because it cannot be: it is pinned.
Work shared privately with the keeper does not enter. Private lanes are counted, not named.

master_invocation_pointer.note: The master invocation is unchanged and is read from the v10.4.0 pin.

lane_mages.$comment: Which mage carries which quest lane and which scroll. The arena seats mages on the lattice; this table joins the quests and scrolls to them.

ages.name: The Age of the Spellbooks
ages.telling: The First Person Spellbook closed at 31 acts, with the Zero, Canon, Parallel and Plurality books beside it. The Privacymage Grimoire carried them, version by version, to v10.4.0, the lattice-coherence edition.

ages.name: The Age of the City
ages.telling: The Second Person Spellbook opened as the City of Mages: workshops, districts, the cast tiers, the Tower, the Hearth and the Wellpool, the Register of Invitations. The City Grimoire carried it to v1.9.3, the three-workings edition.

ages.name: The Age of Evidence
ages.telling: The mages left the page and went to work. Each lane of the dual-agent harness became a mage whose casts are sealed as κ evidence bundles, written on scrolls as nothing but hashes and resolved on the Sigil. The City became a verifiable trust community: what a mage did is a root anyone can check, and what it found stays behind the veil until a reader joins. The research register ruled on the earlier conjectures, and V7 took its first receipts. The record moved faster than the reading: most of this age's chronicles still wait for the First Person's signature.

errata.subject: C4: the 96 edges

earlier.quote: 96 edges encoding 64 vertices. The surface on which blades are ground. C4 resolved.

now.quote: challenged · reopened 2026-10-25: no stated graph on Z/64 has 96 edges (192/64/32/94/95, Lean-checked); 96 is the UOR Atlas vertex count, imported (F6)

errata.reading: C4 is open again. The 96 belongs to the UOR Atlas, not to any graph the grimoire states on the 64 vertices.

errata.subject: C1: the golden ratio as optimum

earlier.quote: The golden ratio emerges as conjectured optimal balance between privacy and delegation.

now.quote: refuted as worded for the stated Φ (min(1,(S/M)/φ) is flat for S/M ≥ φ); restated as a threshold, modelling choice (F2)

errata.reading: φ is a threshold the model chooses, not an optimum it finds.

errata.subject: The strict ceiling R < 1

now.quote: The strict ceiling R < 1 holds exactly when the deficit C_S + C_M < H(X | B) is declared and attested for the deployment.

errata.reading: The ceiling is declared, not derived. It holds for a deployment that declares and attests its deficit, and is not a property of the lattice alone.

errata.subject: The status block of v10.4.0
errata.reading: The v10.4.0 pin's status block still reads version 10.1.0 and the v10.1.0 edition name. The file's own version field is 10.4.0. Read the top-level version.

errata.subject: A home-directory path in narrative_sync

now.quote: The next grimoire (v11) drops the path.

errata.reading: The pins from v10.2.0 to v10.4.0 carry a local folder path. It is sealed as published. v11 carries no local path, and its build fails if one appears.

agreements.subject: C14: the dihedral group core

earlier.quote: The symmetry group generated by two involutions. Algebraic name of the dual-agent architecture. D_2n.

now.quote: the group core ⟨neg,bnot⟩ ≅ D₆₄, order 128, transitive on Z/64, is a theorem with a Lean receipt

agreements.reading: What the grimoire named, the register proved.

open_items: The Zero Spellbook's tale 32, The Flock, is a proposed patch (v10.4.2), not applied: its numbering is stated under two conventions until the author rules.
The City Grimoire's deferred persona reseats under the lattice lock (from v1.8.0) are still not applied to the vertex inventory.
Tome IX acts 6 to 9 are drafts awaiting the First Person's review; Tome XI, The Constellation, is proposed.
Most master chronicles of the Age of Evidence are unsigned. Their inversions enter this grimoire as they are signed.
Half the roster has no seat yet: the mages that hold a scroll or a quest but are not in the arena have no vertex and no patron. The arena seats them.
The bound-collection manifest lags the disk (Tome VII, VIII and IX list fewer acts than are written); each tome's entry here quotes it beside the count on disk.
v11 is a draft. The First Person reviews it, the soul mage censuses it, and only then is it pinned and its CID recorded.

closing.proverb: The seal says what was; the signature says it was read.
